objective: Implement durable private first-frame video posters for new and legacy Community Wall videos across public and exact-scope walls, preserving existing playback, AWS routing, upload limits, offline behavior and ad lifecycle.
productionBaselineEvidence: verified: Android Production OTA run #248 published source SHA 11cf6bd096054dbf8ac204186b199fc835e740e3 on runtime 1.3.2. Current main @ 99cf163691a1cb1e24b3994c3bd44da3ee546a33 is the DEV baseline for this work and is NOT represented as the live production source. No production artifact or runtime is changed by this PR.
chosenApproach: Generate one compact JPEG during Wall upload; attach it through an author-checked RPC into a private sidecar table. Older videos lazily backfill their poster from an already-visible native player through a visibility-checked RPC. Web upload uses a local video/canvas frame capture. The migration also backfills eligible legacy single-video rows into the shared media relation, covering the existing public/scoped legacy posts without rewriting their original storage objects.
selectionRationale: Avoid hidden players and speculative downloads for every feed item while replacing blank inactive video tiles with a useful preview after first viewing.
preserveBehaviors: No hidden/offscreen players or speculative downloads for feed cards
Existing single-player lifecycle, autoplay/viewability and fullscreen sizing
Signed URL refresh and bounded playback retry
Google IMA ads, companion placements and ad events
Private community-media bucket and exact post/scope visibility; no public bucket or public thumbnail URLs
Original video object and 1 GB upload cap remain unchanged
AWS external-video upload route and metadata shape
Bounded 125 KB JPEG poster files and best-effort fallback if poster generation/upload fails
No new native dependencies, package identity, runtime version or production OTA
Legacy-video lazy poster backfill is limited to the post author; other viewers cannot write preview metadata
acceptanceChecks: New public Wall videos generate and upload a private first-frame JPEG no larger than 125 KB
New Organization/Sub-org/Cluster Wall videos generate private posters using the uploader's owner namespace
Existing public and scoped videos lazily persist a poster only after an already-visible player produces a frame
Web uploads can create a first-frame poster without invoking native Expo Video thumbnail APIs
Media RPC v4 returns durable video poster metadata while preserving legacy photo sidecars
Media attachment v6 validates author, media row, JPEG metadata, owner path and 125 KB cap
Lazy registration RPC validates the caller can view the exact post and video position
Storage RLS permits poster reads only when the related post is visible; anon remains denied
Referenced preview objects cannot be deleted through ordinary owner-delete policies
Scope-prefixed Supabase video uploads remain membership-checked and are accepted for supported video MIME types
Poster generation failure never blocks video upload or post publishing
Focused poster tests, Supabase security SQL tests, TypeScript, media regression and engineering accountability gates pass
Physical-device visual, weak-network, memory and IMA playback verification remains an RC gate
Legacy-video lazy backfill is authorized only for the post author and exact visible media position
Eligible legacy single-video Wall records are backfilled into the shared media rows so existing posts can receive author-only lazy posters
alternativeApproaches: Generate hidden players for every feed video (rejected: speculative downloads and decoder/memory pressure).
Make thumbnail objects public (rejected: leaks private organization/cluster media).
Use the legacy photo sidecar table (rejected: its path-derived constraint only supports .jpg image naming).
Add a native module or replace expo-video (rejected: current SDK 57 shared-thumbnail and ImageManipulator APIs already support the required flow).
